outcome: No proof, disproof, partial resolution, or AI-related result affecting Gillies' conjecture on the distribution of prime divisors of Mersenne numbers was found between 26 January 2024 and today; the conjecture remains open with only empirical (pre-2024) support and continues to conflict with the also-open Lenstra–Pomerance–Wagstaff conjecture.
summary: Gillies' conjecture (1964) concerns the distribution of prime divisors of Mersenne numbers M_p = 2^p - 1, modeling divisor counts as approximately Poisson-distributed; it is known to conflict with the widely-accepted but also-open Lenstra–Pomerance–Wagstaff conjecture (predictions differ by about 11%). I checked the current Wikipedia article on the conjecture, which states plainly that it 'remains open' with only empirical support accumulated over past decades, and found no update reflecting any post-January-2024 development. I confirmed the triage's finding that Kovac–Luca's June 2025 arXiv paper 'On the number of divisors of Mersenne numbers' (arXiv:2506.04883) does not touch Gillies' conjecture at all — it proves an unrelated Erdos question, that the ratio f(2n)/f(n) (where f(n) is the cumulative sum of divisor counts τ(2^k-1) for k up to n) is unbounded. This is a genuinely different mathematical object (a cumulative sum of divisor counts across many exponents, not the distribution of prime divisors of a single Mersenne number) and a different question (boundedness of a ratio, not the Poisson-type distributional claim Gillies made), so per §3.1 it is a related problem, not a case of this one, and does not count as a change to this bullet. I found no other papers, preprints, announcements, or discussions from the window that engage with Gillies' specific conjecture, and no mention of any AI system in connection with it. The October 2024 discovery of the 18th Mersenne prime (M136279841, via GIMPS using an Nvidia GPU) is unrelated — it is a single new record prime, not a distributional or divisor-count result, and per §3.1 an existence/discovery event does not move a distributional conjecture. No credible source suggests any AI system has been applied to Gillies' conjecture specifically.
competing_reading: One could argue the Kovac–Luca paper is adjacent enough (same underlying arithmetic function τ(2^k-1), same author lineage citing Gillies' heuristic as motivation) that it constitutes 'progress in the surrounding area,' but it does not change what a careful reader would write in the Gillies'-conjecture bullet itself: the Poisson-type distributional claim about prime divisors of individual Mersenne numbers is untouched, so I do not think this rises even to 'progress' under §3.1.
what_would_settle_it: A paper or preprint since 26 January 2024 that proves, disproves, refines the constant in, or settles a genuine restricted case of Gillies' own distributional/Poisson-model conjecture about prime divisors of M_p, or credible reporting of an AI system being applied to exactly that question.
